messages.content: The airline changed the Milwaukee return and the hospital sent a new construction entrance map. Can you tighten the plan before I start printing everything?

I checked both. The changed Sunday return still leaves MKE at 2:15 p.m., but the ATL connection is down to 36 minutes. I would not risk that after teardown. The cleaner alternate is MKE-DTW-TPA: 1:50 p.m. departure, 76 minutes in Detroit, Tampa at 8:18 p.m., +$42. Seats: free window on MKE-DTW; no free window on DTW-TPA right now, so I can set the alert and skip the paid $21 window.
Switch to Detroit if the rental timing still works. Do not pay for the last window.

It works. You can leave the hotel at 11:25, drop the compact car at the MKE terminal rental center by about 12:05, and still have a safe cushion for the 1:50 departure. I changed the return and added a free-window seat alert for DTW-TPA.
What did the hotel say? I mainly need to know if breakfast and Friday recovery are still okay.

The Residence Inn reconfirmed the queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, microwave, desk, fitness room, and indoor pool. The missing item is still the hot tub. Pool caveat: Friday maintenance pushes pool opening to about 7 p.m., so Friday recovery is possible but not right after class.
And the hospital entrance? Their PDF made it look like the front doors are useless.

Correct. Main visitor doors are closed. Use the Visitor Ramp, park on level 3 or higher, take the elevator to level 2, follow the skywalk to the East Clinical Center security desk, then go to therapy. Thursday badge pickup is at education until 5:30; after that, security holds the envelope. Friday and Saturday use the same entrance.
Can I still keep the Thursday grocery stop?

Yes, but only as Plan A. If you land on time: rental 12:15 to 12:35, hotel bag drop around 1:05, grocery 1:25 to 1:55, hospital badge/materials 2:15 to 3:00. If arrival slips past 1:15, skip groceries and use the lobby market until Friday after class. Morning departures are set: Friday leave hotel 6:55, Saturday leave 7:05. I added the revised map, pool note, and grocery fallback to the trip sheet.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Kara asked for options grouped by practicality, weighed Thursday versus Friday and GSP versus AVL around functional timing, treated pool/hot tub/fitness as important for a hiking recovery weekend, and wanted all-in totals with hotel fees called out before booking.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: Monday afternoon is better than a late-night return.

messages.content: I am ready to look at Asheville for late May. After Milwaukee I want this one to feel like recovery, not another logistics drill. Can you compare it by what is actually practical, not just cheapest?
Yes. Are you thinking Thursday after work to Monday, or Friday morning to Monday? And should I weight walkable dinners downtown against post-hike recovery amenities?

We can do either Thursday after 4:30 or Friday morning. Monday afternoon is better than a late-night return. We want two hikes, probably one Blue Ridge Parkway day, and I do care about a hot tub or pool if the fees are not ridiculous.

Here is the practical flight split. Best breathing room: Thursday evening TPA to Greenville-Spartanburg, connect through ATL, arrive about 9:15 p.m.; Monday GSP to TPA at 2:18 p.m., home about 6:40 p.m., around $338 per person. Cheaper but tighter weekend: Friday morning to GSP, arrive just before noon, same Monday return, around $302 per person. Least driving but weakest schedule: Asheville airport, closer to town, but the Monday options are either too early or get you home near 11 p.m., and fares are closer to $455 per person.
How much worse is Greenville-Spartanburg than Asheville airport once we have a car?

GSP is about 70 to 80 minutes to Asheville on a straightforward interstate drive. AVL is about 20 minutes. Since you will need a car for trailheads either way, GSP mainly adds drive time on arrival and departure. The Monday afternoon GSP flight is the cleanest part of the whole airfare picture.
Okay. Hotel zones next. I do not want a pretty room that is useless after hiking.

Three realistic styles. Downtown Asheville hotel: strongest walkability for meals, 4.6 customer rating, queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, and fitness room, but no pool or hot tub. Mountain lodge near the west side trail access: 4.4 rating, queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, heated pool, hot tub, and small fitness room, but it adds parking plus a resort-style fee and you would drive to dinner. Private cabin near Fairview: kitchenette and privacy, but sparse reviews, no exercise space, and no pool or hot tub.
Give me all-in totals for Thursday versus Friday, including car and the annoying fees.

For May 22 to 26, two adults, before food and gas: Thursday GSP plus downtown hotel plus small SUV is about $2,260. Thursday GSP plus the mountain lodge is about $2,420. Thursday GSP plus the cabin is about $2,190. If you leave Friday instead, each version drops one hotel night and one rental day: downtown about $1,830, lodge about $1,950, cabin about $1,780. The lodge is roughly $160 more than downtown for the Thursday version once parking and resort fees are included.
That is less of a gap than I expected. What exactly are the lodge fees?

The nightly rate is not the whole story. The lodge adds a $32 nightly resort-style fee and $18 nightly parking, plus tax on the room and some fees. For four nights, that is why the quoted room rate looks reasonable but the final hotel total is around $1,430.
Is the rating solid enough? I do not need fancy, but I do not want a tired place with a lukewarm hot tub.

The public rating is 4.4 with a large review count, and recent comments are more positive about the pool and location than about decor. Caveats to verify before booking: hot tub hours, whether the pool is heated in late May, and whether the resort-style fee is refundable if you cancel.
What would you pick if the goal is two hikes and not feeling wrecked Monday night?

I would pick Thursday evening to GSP, the mountain lodge, and a small SUV. It buys you a real Friday instead of a half travel day, keeps the Monday return in the afternoon, and gives you recovery options after hiking. The trade-offs are plain: late drive from GSP Thursday, no walkable dinner scene, and the lodge fees are real. If dinners are the priority, choose downtown. I would drop the cabin unless privacy beats reliability.
Could we stay downtown and just do a spa day pass if we need it?

Possible, but not dependable. Day passes I found run about $45 to $65 per person, and late-evening access is limited. If you use it twice, the downtown savings mostly disappears. Downtown still wins for restaurants and walking; it just does not solve the easy post-hike soak.
What about the car size? Do we need anything more than compact?

A compact would save about $50 to $60. I would still take the small SUV for trailhead comfort, rain gear, and the Parkway day. You do not need a large SUV or guaranteed AWD unless the forecast turns ugly.
Build the tentative plan with the lodge and GSP Thursday, but do not book until I confirm with my partner. Put the hidden fees right next to the hotel total.

Done. Tentative stack only, no holds: Thursday evening TPA-GSP, Monday 2:18 p.m. GSP return, small SUV, and Ridgeline Mountain Lodge queen room. I marked the hotel as about $1,430 all-in, including the $32 nightly resort-style fee and $18 nightly parking. Before booking, I will recheck airfare, hot tub hours, heated pool status, cancellation deadline, and whether any adjacent seats are still available.

Small SUV is $318.40 pay-at-counter. Seats: outbound has adjacent 14A and 14B with one window included. Return has free adjacent 20B and 20C, or paid 12A and 12B with a window for $39 each.
Keep the return free adjacent pair. I would rather not pay $78 just for the window on the way home. On the outbound, put me in the window if that works.

Works. I have you in 14A and your partner in 14B outbound. Return would be 20B and 20C, adjacent but no window. The lodge also reconfirmed the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, heated pool, hot tub from 4 to 10 p.m., and small fitness room. Cancellation is free until May 16 at 6 p.m. local.
Good. Add the late arrival note to the lodge. We will not get there until close to 10:45.

Added. They said the desk is staffed until midnight, and after-hours instructions can be texted if the flight slips. One caveat before I book: the resort-style fee and parking are collected by the lodge and are part of the total, not optional charges.
Understood. Use the saved card and skip travel insurance unless the car needs something prepaid.
Using the saved card for flights and hotel. No travel insurance added. The car is pay-at-counter, and I am not preselecting rental insurance or fuel. Do you want me to complete all three now?
Yes, book it.

Booked the flights: confirmation ASH-GSP-5831. Thursday TPA-ATL-GSP arrives 9:14 p.m.; Monday GSP-ATL-TPA arrives 6:38 p.m. Seats are 14A and 14B outbound, 20B and 20C return. I also booked Ridgeline Mountain Lodge: confirmation RIDGE-6248, queen room, May 22 to 26, late-arrival note added, total $1,432.62 with the parking and resort-style fee included.
And the car?

Booked the small SUV at GSP: confirmation GSP-SUV-3094, pickup Thursday 9:45 p.m., return Monday 11:30 a.m., estimated $318.40 pay-at-counter. Watch items: check in 24 hours before departure in case a free return window opens, cancel the lodge by May 16 at 6 p.m. local if plans change, and leave Asheville around 10:30 Monday for the GSP return so the drive and car drop-off stay calm.
